card.intuition: A ticket is a handoff artifact scoping one session of work, standing alone or hanging off a spec. Tickets can block or be blocked by siblings, so the order of work falls out of their dependency graph rather than a linear plan. Its defining constraint is size: a ticket must be completable before the session drifts out of the smart zone, and that constraint is testable by observing how sessions behave.
card.analogy: A kanban card for a single work item: the card carries the goal and acceptance criteria, and the board orders cards by dependency rather than by who grabbed them first.
card.time_complexity: The model is stateless, so each ticket's carried context costs tokens on every request — right-sized tickets keep per-session spend inside the smart zone.
card.space_complexity: A ticket is sized to fit comfortably in one finite context window, leaving room for the actual work rather than setup overhead.
when_to_use: Scoping one session of work that fits inside the smart zone
Ordering work by a dependency graph instead of a linear plan
Running independent leaf tickets in parallel sessions with multiple agents
Splitting tickets whose sessions routinely degrade before the work is done
gotchas: Too big: sessions degrade before the work is done — split the ticket
Too small: sessions spend most of the context on setup — merge the tickets
Write for a reader with no other context, or the session will re-derive what the last one knew

steps.label: Scope one session
steps.annotation: A ticket scopes exactly one session, with the goal and acceptance criteria written for a reader with no other context.

steps.label: Add context pointers
steps.annotation: The ticket carries pointers to the relevant files and decisions so the session can start working immediately.

steps.label: Build dependency graph
steps.annotation: Tickets that block or are blocked form a dependency graph, so the order of work falls out of it.

steps.label: Run the leaves
steps.annotation: Independent leaf tickets can each run in their own session at the same time.

steps.label: Right-size tickets
steps.annotation: If sessions degrade before finishing, split; if they spend most of context on setup, merge.

exercise.prompt: Complete can_run_in_parallel so it returns True only for a ticket that is a leaf of the dependency graph, with no blockers.
hints: Leaves of the dependency graph have no blockers and can run in parallel.
A ticket without dependencies is ready to run immediately in its own session.
exercise.test_code:
deps = {'A': ['B']}
assert can_run_in_parallel('A', deps) is False
assert can_run_in_parallel('B', deps) is True
print('PASS')
